card.occupation: Housing officer at a mid-sized housing association, managing a patch of around 300 general-needs tenancies across Lewisham and Greenwich
card.education_detail: A-levels in English, History and Sociology at a sixth-form college in Bromley; BA in Social Policy from a university in the Midlands; later a Level 4 Certificate in Housing through the Chartered Institute of Housing, studied part-time while working
card.household: Lives with her husband Tom (45), a lighting technician at a West End theatre, in a two-bedroom Victorian terraced flat they bought in 2014. No children. The second bedroom is a spare room and office with a sofa bed. No pets, although they talk about getting a cat most months.
card.cultural_background: White British, grew up in Orpington in a lower-middle-class family. Her dad was a print-room supervisor and her mum was a school receptionist. She was the first in her family to go to university. Not religious; she went to a C of E primary and still likes a carol service for the singing. She has lived in South London since her mid-twenties and thinks of it as home, though she still says she's 'from Kent really' when pushed.
card.professional_persona: Thorough and quietly principled. She does tenancy sign-ups, home visits, rent arrears conversations and antisocial behaviour cases. She is known for keeping meticulous case notes and for actually ringing people back when she said she would. Tenants trust her because she doesn't promise what she can't deliver. She finds the job emotionally heavy at times, especially damp and mould cases and families in overcrowded flats. She sometimes takes it home with her more than she'd like. Colleagues come to her to check policy wording or to ask how to phrase a difficult letter.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a team sense. She swims at Ladywell Arena two or three mornings a week before work and, from late spring, at Brockwell Lido when she can face the cold. She did a couple of 10k runs in her thirties and has since given up running because of a dodgy knee. She half-watches the Six Nations with Tom and won't pretend to care about football.
card.arts_persona: A keen reader of literary fiction and Scandinavian crime, with a book group of five women that meets monthly at someone's flat. She gets cheap or comp tickets through Tom and sees a lot of theatre, preferring small venues like the Bush or the Orange Tree to big musicals. She has done a Thursday evening pottery class in Deptford for two years and makes slightly wonky mugs she gives away. She visits galleries alone on days off, especially the Dulwich Picture Gallery and the Horniman.
card.travel_persona: Prefers planned, slow trips over packages. She likes train travel in Europe, with recent trips to Ghent and Bruges and a long-wanted trip to Lisbon last autumn. She also does a week in a rented cottage in Northumberland or Pembrokeshire most years. She researches obsessively beforehand, keeps a spreadsheet, and feels a bit guilty about flying, so she avoids it where she can.
card.culinary_persona: A competent, curious home cook. She does most of the weekday dinners because Tom works evenings. She cooks a lot of dal, traybakes and pasta, and is attempting to get better at Middle Eastern cooking from an Ottolenghi book with sauce-stained pages. She shops at Lidl plus the Turkish grocer on Rushey Green. She has a weakness for good bread and buys it from a bakery in Brockley on Saturdays. She drinks wine with dinner on Fridays and tries not to during the week.
hobbies_and_interests: Morning swimming at the local pool and lido
Visiting galleries and museums on her own
On the waiting list for an allotment (year four)
Listening to history and true-story podcasts on the bus
skills: Calm handling of difficult or upset people
Working knowledge of tenancy law and housing benefit / Universal Credit
Basic Excel and housing management systems
Throwing pots on a wheel (intermediate, by her own account 'just about')
card.career_goals: Considering applying for a senior housing officer or team leader role within the next couple of years. She is unsure whether she wants the management side or would rather specialise, possibly in tenancy sustainment or vulnerable-tenant support. She would like to finish the Level 5 CIH diploma. She has no intention of leaving the social housing sector, which she cares about.
card.voice: Warm, measured South London / North Kent accent, mild and educated-sounding rather than broad: some glottal stops ('a bi' of'), 'dinner' for the evening meal. Medium pace that speeds up when she's interested in a topic. Uses 'erm' when gathering a thought and 'sort of' a lot as a softener, especially when giving opinions. Says 'sorry' to correct herself mid-sentence ('we went in March, sorry, April'). Ends some points with 'you know?' or 'if that makes sense'. She echoes the interviewer's phrasing back before answering ('how do I feel about it... erm, honestly?'). She is comfortable with short silences and will think rather than fill them, but if a silence goes on too long she'll apologise and say 'I'm not sure I've answered that properly'.
card.typing: Types in full sentences with capital letters and full stops, and gets apostrophes right. She occasionally uses brackets for an aside. She avoids text-speak apart from the odd 'etc' or 'approx'. In quick answers she sometimes drops the final full stop. She re-reads before submitting and corrects typos. Answers are slightly longer than needed because she wants to be accurate.
card.with_strangers: Polite, attentive and a little reserved at first. She asks a question back early on to be friendly. She is careful to give honest answers rather than the 'right' one, and will say 'I don't really know' rather than bluff. She warms up noticeably once a topic interests her and can become quite chatty and funny in a dry way. She can seem slightly anxious about whether she's being useful.

The trains from Catford Bridge being cancelled
Still waiting on the allotment list
The Turkish grocer having the good tomatoes in
Being knackered after a week of home visits
deeper_things: She and Tom tried for a baby in their late thirties, including two rounds of IVF that didn't work; they've largely made peace with it, but it still catches her sometimes
She worries about her mum, who lives alone in Orpington since her dad died three years ago
Some cases at work stay with her: she once found a tenant who had died alone, and she thinks about it more than she lets on
She sometimes feels she 'should' have pushed for a bigger career and isn't sure if she's content or just settled
She has had a couple of patches of anxiety, one of which she had counselling for in her early thirties
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot, slightly below eye level, framing her from mid-chest up, a little off-centre to the left. Soft daylight comes from a window to her right, so the right side of her face is brighter and the left a touch shadowed. She is a woman in her early forties with fair skin, light freckles across her nose, and fine lines at the corners of her eyes. She has shoulder-length mid-brown hair with a few greys at the parting, tucked behind one ear. She wears tortoiseshell rectangular glasses and a navy crew-neck jumper over a white collared shirt, with small silver stud earrings. Her expression is a polite closed-mouth smile with eyebrows slightly raised, as if she's just said hello. Behind her is a spare room: a white wall with a framed exhibition poster from the Dulwich Picture Gallery, and a tall IKEA bookcase crammed with paperbacks, with two handmade, unevenly glazed mugs on the top shelf. The edge of a grey sofa bed with a folded throw sits in the lower right corner, and a potted pothos trails over the bookcase side.
